newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia opposition urges interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia opposition urges interest rate cut.

text.p: Australian opposition leader Kim Beazley on Tuesday urged the Reserve Bank of Australia to cut interest rates further.
"Interest rates should come down," Beazley told reporters.
The bank board is meeting in Sydney, amid market speculation of a possible interest rate cut.
"We licked inflation when we were in office and the product of licked inflation is low interest rates," Beazley said.
"There is room for those interest rates to come down."
Beazley's Labor Party was dumped from power in a March, 1996, election after 13 years in office.
Beazley said the bank did not need to wait for the outcome of a national union wage claim before cutting rates again, because low inflation was locked in and the economy could sustain the increase.

The peak union body, the Australian Council of Trade Unions, is seeking an 8.75 percent increases in award wages for workers not covered by workplace agreements and three A$20 a week safety net increases over three years.
The RBA has cut rates a total 1.5 percentage points since July, 1996.
The official overnight cash rate now stands a 6.0 percent.
